title: Two dials, one position

text.guided:
A drone has two thrusters, u and v. Turn dial **a** and it moves a times along u; turn dial **b** and it moves b times along v. Its final position is the **linear combination** a·u + b·v.

For example, with u = (1, 0) and v = (0, 1), the combination 2u + 3v is the point (2, 3).
text.fast: A linear combination is $a\,u + b\,v$. With the standard basis, $2\hat\imath + 3\hat\jmath = (2, 3)$.

examples.games: A hero moves with two keys: how many steps right and how many steps up give the position.
examples.physics: Two forces along different directions combine into one resultant force.
examples.sport: Your position on the pitch = a steps along the touchline + b steps towards goal.

robot: This drone has only two thrusters. Mix them and it goes anywhere, or almost.

mission.games: Dial the two thrusters so the drone grabs the power-up on (2, 2).
mission.physics: Two engines, u = (1, 0) and v = (0, 1). Reach the beacon on (2, 2).
mission.sport: Run a steps along the touchline and b steps up the pitch to reach the ball on (2, 2).

title: Any two arrows will do

text.guided:
u and v do not have to be perpendicular. As long as they are not on the same line, you can reach **every** point of the plane by choosing the right a and b, and a can be negative to run a thruster backwards.

In the picture, î stands for u = (1, 1) and ĵ for v = (1, −1).
text.fast: Any two linearly independent vectors span the plane. Coefficients may be negative or fractional.

examples.games: Two diagonal buttons can still reach any tile, if you may press them a negative number of times.
examples.physics: Any two non-parallel directions are enough to express a force.
examples.sport: Two diagonal runs, forward-left and forward-right, still cover the whole pitch if you may also run them backwards.

robot: Tilted thrusters still cover the plane. You may need to fire one backwards.

mission.games: Diagonal thrusters only. Reach the checkpoint on (3, 1).
mission.physics: Thrust along (1, 1) and (1, -1) to dock on (3, 1).
mission.sport: Two diagonal runs, (1, 1) and (1, -1). Meet the cross on (3, 1).

title: When the thrusters line up

text.guided:
If u and v point along the **same line**, every combination stays on that line, however you turn the dials. A target off the line is **unreachable**.

So before you turn any dial, check: is v a multiple of u? If it is, only targets on that line can be reached.
text.fast: If $v = ku$, the span is a line. Targets off that line are unreachable.

examples.games: Two buttons that both move you diagonally up-right can never take you straight up.
examples.physics: Two forces on the same line can never produce a sideways force.
examples.sport: Two players who can only run along the same diagonal can never reach a ball straight to the side.

robot: Two thrusters on the same line give one line, no more. Some targets are just out of reach.

check.prompt: u = (1, 2) and v = (2, 4). Can the drone reach the point (1, 0)?
options: Yes, with enough of both thrusters
No: both thrusters only move along the same line
